conventions.convention: The equation-based model adopts smooth fields on an open subset of an oriented, time-oriented, boundaryless Lorentzian four-manifold with signature (-,+,+,+). Every matter instance must specify its configurations, equations, constraints, current map and stress map; arbitrary independently chosen current and stress are insufficient.
The sourced Maxwell sign is ∇a F^{ab} = −μ0 j^b, and electromagnetic stress is μ0^{-1}(F_ac F_b{}^c − g_ab F_cd F^{cd}/4). The Einstein coupling is κE = 8π GN/c^4 with constant Λ.

Normalized connection representatives a_i give physical potentials A_i = κ0 a_i and physical curvature F = κ0 da_i. A physical connection variation α changes a_i by α/κ0, preserves transitions and gives δF = dα. The matter variation is −(2c)^{-1}∫T^m_ab δg^{ab} vol_g + c^{-1}∫j^a α_a vol_g.

Action stationarity uses independent smooth compactly supported interior metric, fixed-sector connection and matter variations. Noncompact actions are interpreted through compact action differences. No boundary variational principle or solution-existence assertion follows.

Restricted dust has constant m > 0 and real q, smooth positive proper number density ν, future velocity U with g(U,U) = −c², current qνU and stress mνU⊗U. Number continuity and the Lorentz-force equation are independently adopted continuum equations.

The scalar action is exactly the earlier functional Sφ. Its circle-bundle branch requires λκ0 = k ∈ ℤ; its separate trivial global-real-potential branch permits any real λ. Kφ is positive, V is real and smooth near attained squared amplitudes, and no quantum mass interpretation is imposed.
The compact-integration supplier chain assumes Countable Choice: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function. No full Axiom of Choice is claimed.

load_bearing.statement: For the smooth fixed-sector action and selected matter functional of post-emg-einstein-maxwell-action, stationarity under every admissible compact metric, connection and matter variation is equivalent to the sourced Maxwell equation, G_ab + Λg_ab = κE(T^EM_ab + T^m_ab), and vanishing selected matter variation in every admissible compact direction. The curvature also satisfies dF = 0.

Select one actual differentiable matter functional on the declared smooth fixed-bundle domain, invariant under the specified gauge transformations and transported diffeomorphisms, with matter stationarity and the stated physical-connection/current and inverse-metric/Hilbert first-variation conventions.
For an explicitly specified admissible smooth matter-model instance, adopt dF = 0, ∇a F^{ab} = −μ0j^b and G_ab + Λg_ab = κE(T^EM_ab + T^m_ab), independently of a matter action.

For the specified smooth scalar action, scalar stationarity is equivalent to Eφ = D_aP^a − V'(|φ|²)φ = 0. Full action stationarity yields Maxwell and Einstein equations with the displayed scalar current and Hilbert stress; on the scalar equation, ∇a j^a = 0 and ∇a(Tφ)^a{}_b = F_ba j^a.

For the same smooth selected invariant matter action and connection, with matter on shell and the adopted Maxwell equations, ∇a T_EM^{ab} = −F^{bc}j_c, ∇a T_m^{ab} = F^{bc}j_c, and ∇a(T_EM^{ab} + T_m^{ab}) = 0. With the constant-Λ Einstein equation, this is its necessary Bianchi source-compatibility condition.

published_dependencies.used_for: Smooth oriented Lorentzian geometry, observer and frame definitions, curvature contractions, length-coordinate bookkeeping and inherited Countable Choice convention.
Exact inverse-metric Hilbert variation convention, including its sign, factor 1/(2c), fixed matter configuration and admitted compact metric directions.
Earlier flat field and prescribed-potential particle stationarity context; the assigned action postulate correctly states that this supplier does not provide a unified curved matter–gravity action.
Exact indexed Countable Choice assumption carried by the action and compact-integration arguments.
Contracted identity ∇^a G_ab = 0 for the metric-selected Lorentzian connection, giving necessary total-source compatibility when Λ is constant.
Dust Lorentz-force sign and four-velocity normalization context only; its finite prescribed-background particle theorem is not used to derive continuum continuity or existence.

concerns.concern: The Carroll locator describes Chapter 4 equations (4.69)–(4.72) as 'electromagnetic stress'. Those equations concern general metric variation, Hilbert stress, canonical stress and the weak energy condition; the electromagnetic expression appears at (1.111). Verified against [Carroll's cited manuscript](https://arxiv.org/pdf/gr-qc/9712019v1), printed pp. 116–117 and 30. The local proof uses adequate explicit mathematical suppliers, so this is a source-description defect.

The Carroll locator calls Chapter 4 equations (4.69)–(4.72) 'Maxwell stress and Einstein coupling'. The coupling and general Hilbert convention occur there, but Maxwell stress does not; see (1.111), printed p. 30, in [the cited manuscript](https://arxiv.org/pdf/gr-qc/9712019v1). The counterexample's explicit stress computation is sound independently of this inaccurate locator.

seams_checked.note: Preserves the smooth SI geometry, field/current dictionary and negative sourced-Maxwell sign. Curved field adoption remains a postulate, without importing a global flat metric or global potential.

The inspected Einstein, Noether, scalar and electromagnetic-divergence suppliers support the stated compact variations, normalizations and opposite exchange signs. Their conditional hypotheses are retained.
The charged-fluid development uses the equation-based postulate with an explicitly supplied fluid closure, matching current, stress and field equations; it assumes no matter action.

Electrovacuum consumers select the singleton zero functional, retain fixed normalized bundle compatibility, and use both directions of the action-field equivalence. Existence comes from separate mathematical development suppliers.

The global-real-potential scalar model matches the smooth action coefficients while separately adopting its finite-regularity domain and proving variations there; it does not attribute that extension to the smooth supplier.

Transported dust and fluid branches state their own closures and use the equation-based Einstein–Maxwell system. They do not claim that the restricted constant-parameter dust definition supplies these broader models.

RN and KN consumers use the zero-matter equation-based specialization with Λ = 0 and the same electromagnetic stress and κE. Their solution claims remain conditional on separately named mathematical verification suppliers.
